notes: Ran the brief recordBriefCommand actually emits (`;`, not REFERENCE.md's `&&`): `[ -f m ] || tp audit --merge abad.ndjson -o m; tp audit a.md --record m`. The merge exits 1 and still writes a zero-byte -o (line 119); --record then reports round 1 clean:true, consecutive_clean:1, and the chain exits 0. Two of those converge — the exact failure §5 row 10 fixed for review. §4 fences the code change and lines 115-118 say so honestly, but no document states this consequence of the emitted `;` form.

`-o` naming an existing directory on an otherwise succeeding merge: HEAD gives `cannot write output file: rename ./outdir.tp-merge-3626064968 outdir: file exists`, hint `check -o/--output: its directory must exist and be writable` — the directory exists and is writable, and the temp path is already gone. Built bcf5bf3b^ and ran the same input: `open outdirA: is a directory`. The new temp+rename shape routes every -o failure through rename, so no -o error is self-explanatory now.

codeAuditOutputFormat declares NDJSON, then ends `If no issues found, respond with an empty array (just [])`. Ran it: a file holding `[]` makes --merge warn malformed, exit 1 and write no -o (§5 row 10), hint blaming JSON framing — sibling roles' rows go with it. Every other emitted format says `zero lines`. Also outputContractInstruction (1137-1161) says `stamp EVERY finding with the full contract` and lists role/location/class/severity: no evidence, no finding.

The skip warning names the key and the file but never the line, while --record names `line N:`. A five-row file gave five byte-identical-but-for-the-key warnings with no way to locate them. It also reports `missing evidence` for an evidence of 42, of [x], of null and of {} — present, not a string (missingFindingFields' type assertion). §2 shares the predicate; the two gates' diagnostics do not share locatability, and evidence is the key most likely to arrive non-string.

A row carrying severity high, finding f1, location §1 and evidence 42 (a JSON number) gives exit 1 with `line 1: missing required field evidence` and a hint naming the same four keys. The row carries evidence and it is non-empty; the value is not a string. Same for array, object and null — four rows measured. Neither message nor hint says the value must be a JSON string, so the next edit repeats it. The gate itself is right: all five offending lines named in one exit.

verifyOutputFormat now requires evidence — I parsed the emitted object line and it carries severity/finding/location/evidence — but verifyFinding declares no Evidence field, so buildVerifyPrompt never shows it. Measured: a findings file whose two rows hold an evidence string EVIDENCE-RAN-TP-LINT produced a prompt containing the finding text and resolved.evidence and neither top-level evidence. The pass told to confirm findings are still present never sees what was run.

The docstring says the scanned columns are those whose header `contains the word fixture or the word mutant once lowercased. Containment rather than equality`, but _header_columns does whole-word membership over re.findall of [a-z]+. A Tests table with headers `fixtures`/`mutants`, both cells citing `the measurements file`: exit 0, `scanned 0 Tests-table row(s) across 0 file(s)`. Singular headers, same cells: exit 1, two problems. It fails open and looks clean.

The line claims a line past the 1MB per-line NDJSON cap exits 3 `at every reader in the review/audit family (--merge, --report, --resolve, --verify, --record, and tp audit --findings)`. Measured with a 1.5MB single-line row: --merge 3, --resolve 3, --verify 3, but `tp review <spec> --record` exits 0 and records the round — parseRecordRows uses strings.SplitSeq, no cap — and --report over that round exits 0 too.

SKILL.md never names v1.1.0's required set: zero lines naming severity/finding/location/evidence as required, zero for `skips a row` or `incomplete line`. Review-loop steps 3-4 (268-273, edited by 6b78bd02 in this release) state the -o rule and not the key rule; line 742's `Evidence demand` says `a location and a why`, not the key. An agent driving the loop from the skill alone writes rows --record refuses. REFERENCE.md:740 carries it; the skill ships alone to non-Claude runtimes.

Both checks resolve their spec via `tp resume | python ...[spec]` with 2>/dev/null, so they depend on the git-ignored .tp/local.json. Measured in a fresh `git clone --no-hardlinks`: resume returns `no task file found`, the substitution is empty, the check script exits 2 (`no such spec: `). tp suppresses anyway — `tp review --role implementer` printed `do NOT report findings of these classes: code-citation-drift, method-only-in-ungraded-sidecar`, mechanical_checks absent.

os.WriteFile(outputPath,...,0o600) at :119 sets the mode only when it CREATES the file. Ran: with -o an existing 0644 file, tp audit --merge overwrote it and left -rw-r--r--, while the review path's CreateTemp+rename always lands at 0600 — the two merges now disagree on -o's permission and the :115-118 comment documents only the write-before-refuse half of the asymmetry. Documented half verified too: exit 1 with the seed replaced by the surviving row.

writeMergeOutput:78 swallows os.Remove's error, and :54-56 claims unqualified that a failed write leaves no temporary beside -o. Ran: chflags uchg on the temp mid-write — rename EPERM, Remove EPERM, a 135MB out.ndjson.tp-merge-* left beside -o and named nowhere in the error; SIGKILL mid-write leaves the same orphan and nothing sweeps it. Also new: the sibling temp needs dir-write permission and ~20 bytes of name headroom, so a 236-byte -o basename that merged at v1.0.1 now exits 3.

review_merge.go:47-50 drops a row on a json.Marshal error with a bare continue and no warning, while the sibling audit_merge.go:51-55 warns on the identical branch. The row still counts in merged_count, so -o and the summary would disagree in silence. Not reachable on today's inputs (every value comes from json.Unmarshal, plus an int and a []string), hence info: the repair is the missing warning, not the control flow.

parseRecordRows reads with strings.SplitSeq (uncapped) while every merge/resolve/report reader caps at ndjsonLineCap; the shared-cap guard test walks only bufio.NewScanner sites, so it cannot see this one, though ndjsonLineCap's comment claims every NDJSON reader. Ran: a row with 1.1MB evidence records at exit 0, then --resolve and --report on tp's own review-round-1.ndjson both exit 3 token-too-long — the round cannot be dispositioned. §2's mandatory free-text evidence makes it reachable.

REFERENCE.md:182's rewritten brief_command leaves $TP_ROUND_DIR unquoted. Ran under sh: unset, the guard becomes [ -f /merged.ndjson ] -> false, so the chain merges to -o /merged.ndjson at the root; with a space in the path the guard is a syntax error (exit 2) not a false, and role-*.ndjson word-splits into two argv entries. Separately :687 still says "Both merges apply the rule identically", which :198-200 and :1100-1107 of this same file now contradict.

SKILL.md:272 states the -o rule generally ("-o writes only when the merge succeeds") and :383/:638 apply -o to tp audit --merge without the caveat; only REFERENCE.md:1105 says the audit merge still writes -o before exiting 1. Ran both: tp audit --merge over a seeded -o exited 1 and replaced the seed with the surviving row, while tp review --merge left an identically seeded path untouched. A reader using SKILL.md alone branches the audit chain on file presence and records a stale round.

findingFormat:809 now requires severity, finding, location, evidence. outputContractInstruction, appended right after it at :1121 and at review_regression.go:196, calls itself 'the full contract' and lists role, location, class, severity - omitting evidence and finding. Its doc comment 1130-1136 repeats that. The closure excused it as shared with the auditors, but it already branches on phase at 1143/1146, so the review branch is changeable alone.
